Since its oil and natural gas reserves have long since been depleted, the large cities and factories here rely heavily on geothermal and wind energy. One fortunate side effect of that is that the air here is almost as pristine as on a non-industrial world.

spaceport.text: The largest hangars in the spaceport are built of metal beams more than a meter wide, with thick glass panels between them to let in the sunlight. Even the smaller and newer warehouses on the outskirts of the port seem as solid and permanent as the mountains themselves. Thousands of Hai are walking back and forth between the buildings, and many of them regard you with curiosity; there are very few human visitors here.

description.text: Tens of thousands of Hai pass through on an almost daily basis as the continual churn of summits, forums, conventions, symposiums, productions, conferences, weddings, festivals, and the like roll on in an endless cavalcade of life. With Icelake nearby and Hai-home just one jump away, this station is a major cultural hub that even houses the head office of one of the biggest music labels in Hai space.

spaceport.text: The spaceport promenade runs around the interior of the station and is divided into the usual two levels, but has four additional ring levels rising up from the promenade into each of the station's main branches. Almost any business or service you could want can be found here - except for an outfitter or shipyard. Apparently there is simply no room, as the docking bay must take up nearly all the station's exterior space to accommodate its massive volume of daily traffic.

description.text: The deserts are hot in daylight and surprisingly cool at night, and as a result most settlers live in houses sunk into the ground in regions where there is enough plant cover to keep the dunes from shifting in the wind and slowly burying their dwellings.

spaceport.text: Under the clear sky and with white sand in all directions, the sunlight is painfully bright, and you have been warned to avoid prolonged exposure to it.

description.text: Cattle handlers here do their work on horseback, because they believe modern vehicles are more likely to spook the animals.

spaceport.text: The Grange is currently set up for Remembrance Day celebrations. The population inside consists mostly of the older residents of the planet, many of them likely having traveled tens of thousands of kilometers to arrive here.

description.text: Although the Hai tend to be an easygoing and nonviolent species, there are always a few in each generation that yearn for excitement, warfare, and conquest. These "Unfettered" Hai have built a major military base here, and they launch raids from here on convoys traveling through the nearby systems.

spaceport.text: It is likely that most of the goods available for trade here were stolen from one of the nearby Hai systems.

description.text: As far as desert worlds come, Amathil is merely dry and sandy, with a mild surface temperature that is surprisingly uniform across latitudes thanks to high altitude winds. While unattractive for settlement due to the scarcity of greenery, Amathil is still home to the descendents of those who arrived on the first few sublight starships, back when little was known about the planet besides that it had an oxygenated atmosphere. The unique culture that has since grown here, under a unified planetary government, emphasizes a sense of community and generosity - or at least that is how the locals like to be perceived by outsiders.

spaceport.text: Thanks to its abundant solar energy, the cost of powering the laser launch array that served Amathil was quite low, and glittering fields of solar panels surround the entire site. The spaceport itself is spartan, with Amathil not receiving much traffic on a daily basis even before the Incursion. Amathil's primary export was people, with many choosing to leave the isolated planet in favor of moving to one of the more cosmopolitan worlds elsewhere.

description.text: Glory is also home to the Academy of Planetary Sciences, the organization at the forefront of terraforming research. The Academy takes on only a handful of apprentices each year, and guards its secrets very closely.

spaceport.text: It is almost impossible to tell the age of the locals who are walking by: there is a frightening monotony of wrinkle-free, nearly identically proportioned faces. When they speak, only their lips move; their expressions remain mask-like, immobile.

description.text: The abandoned villages and towns are now buried deep beneath the snow, and occasional treasure hunters come here to explore them and find items of value that were left behind.

As with all refineries in the Deep, Phoenix Station is government-owned. You cannot imagine who would want to live here; despite reflective hull plating and active cooling systems, the station is uncomfortably hot. Nearly all the work is done by robots and computers, with only a skeleton crew of people supervising. Every time the station's orbit brings it through the planet's shadow, the temperature drops briefly and the entire station creaks ominously as it cools.
Settlements show up as small bright points on the dark side of the planet - not from city lights, but from natural gas burnoff at the drilling stations.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is in the middle of a field of oil derricks so vast that from above, the desert seemed to be covered in spiky gray fur. The spaceport itself is a soaring canopy, made to look like a tent, or sails on a ship. But it is built of a sturdy composite of plastic and carbon fiber, and coated in reflective plastic. Inside, hovercraft and massive sand-crawlers are bringing cargo to and from the refineries and factories scattered across the planet's surface.

description.text: Although preservation is a primary goal, the Scin still manipulate the planet for the sake of research. Even if it's not harming the environment directly, patches of the planet have been converted into large experimentation grounds, some a bit less humane than others.

spaceport.text: The spaceport you are staying at is one huge circular construction outfitted with strange looking devices and technology, very much in contrast to the surrounding natural environment. In an open section located at the center is a small forest being observed by the nearby Scin. Some of them, however, seem to be more interested in observing you.

description.text: Cipi's forests and mountains are a suitable place for the Gegno Scin's less active population, home to more quiet industries. The population of this planet is limited, and architecture is built high in mountain ranges to avoid hurting the natural landscapes of the planet. This provides the Scin with healthy crop and hunting seasons to supply their main population without the interference of polluting industry.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is built protruding off the side of a mountain, supported underneath by several pylons in a half-oval formation. The valley down below is extremely narrow, which seems to invite Scin fighters to test their skills. You spot a few Halites zipping through the valley while dodging between the supporting pylons before pulling upward and flying past the edge of the port. Despite their speed, they are not particularly loud.

description.text: On this mining world, the Hai are using boring machines to drill tunnels straight into the hearts of the mountains. Each tunnel twists and turns to intersect the regions of rock with the highest concentrations of valuable ore. Most of the tunnels also join up with other tunnels that have been dug through the same mountains, so that there are multiple exits from any given point in the mines.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is in the center of one of the large cities that are built high up in the mountains where the air is cooler. It consists mostly of open-air landing pads: enormous slabs of metal embedded into the mountainside at different levels, with winding roads connecting them to the main marketplace and warehouse district. Several old mine entrances, well reinforced with metal struts, have been converted into hangar bays or warehouse space.

description.text: Despite the Hai's notably durable engineering, this station appears to have sustained substantial damage since it was abandoned. Given its proximity to Unfettered space, the station's scars are most likely a reflection of the current war taking place between the Hai and their northern brethren.

However, there are some conspicuous areas of leveled ground large enough to build cities on scattered across the planet's surface. The heat at the equator is too hot for a human to visit. While you can survive here, you do not see any wildlife in this harsh environment.

spaceport.text: None of them speak to you, but a worker in the spaceport digs around in a closet for a while and comes up with a conversion attachment that allows your fuel tanks to be filled using their style of fuel nozzle. When asked about this, the worker merely points at the number "42" engraved on the nozzle handle...

description.text: The Quarg here seem different from the other Quarg you've met. Their clothes bear colorful accents and their skin flashes with colorful expression. Those you speak with are eager to learn of how the rest of their species fares back in the Milky Way. Much of their activities in this region are divided between monitoring Cthogha, searching for resources, or general research of this proto-galaxy.

spaceport.text: All of the Quarg ships you see are exotic designs radically different from what is normally seen in Quarg fleets. The station itself is clean, but there are clear signs of wear and neglect.

description.text: Cities with impossibly high towers, connected by arches and bridges, are sprinkled across the landscape, and surrounding the cities are shorter, uglier buildings used as factories. A large amount of the land area is unsettled, its natural beauty untouched. By all appearances, this planet is an exact duplicate of Pugglemug.

spaceport.text: The primary spaceport here is marked by an enormous collection of arches forming an open-air dome. Based on the power cables and devices attached to the sides of the arches, you suspect that the entire dome can be protected by an energy shield if necessary. Inside it, landing platforms jut out from the arches at many different levels.

description.text: Much of the planet's surface is covered by a sea of molten lava. The extreme heat is uncomfortable even for the Ignitia. Only a few settlements were established here, despite the close proximity to their homeworld.

The rocky surface of this planet is covered by rivers of hot magma. No human could survive here and the hulls of most starships would start to melt before they landed. The intensity of the heat is too much for your scanners to make any readings and it's impossible for you to observe anything with your own eyes without being charred to a crisp.

This rocky world is unsettled by the Ignitia. A mining operation here would be able to tap into the planet's rich mineral deposits. While the climate is moderately cool by human standards, the Ignitia are likely to find it inhospitable.

description.text: The first world settled by the Justicar was where the first penal processing center was constructed for all who disobeyed the edicts of the Justicar Court. Convictions have tapered off over the years as the rate of crime decreased.

The surface of the Justicar homeworld is cold and lifeless. The population appears to have been completely replaced by machines. The Grand Jury of the Justicar Court convenes here to deliberate disagreements regarding law and order. The decisions made here dictate the Justicar Code of Conduct at all levels in their society.

port.description: Steel and glass cover every surface. It is all meticulously clean and sterile. From a distance, the rest of the planet is no different. While there are androids, robots, and drones going about their business, you see no living natives.

description.text: Most Urd miners are descendants of refugees from the Alpha War who were granted sanctuary by the pirate lords of Skuld. They aren't slaves. But they are expected to pay tribute for "protection". While some resent being born into this way of life, most here accept it.

spaceport.text: The landing strip ends with a gigantic tunnel that allows ships to be parked underground. Much of the rest of the spaceport consists of a series of subterrainian passages and artificially constructed caverns.

description.text: When humans first arrived in Archipelago they learned that the alien device orbiting the largest star could shut down the Hyperspace links to the star cluster. Over the centuries, the Archipelago would turn into the galaxy's best secret hideout for pirates and anarchists. The almost Earth-like environment of Skuld makes it a perfect rendezvous point for the rare instance when different pirate factions need a place to host a council.

spaceport.text: The buildings surrounding the spaceport were converted from the hulls of multiple ancient city ships. Despite this, it is relatively modern for a pirate world. Few of the other pirate spaceports you've visited are as well stocked and equipped. There are enough landing pads to handle traffic for multiple large fleets.

description.text: Featuring thick forests nestled between mountains dotted with caves, Verdandi is an ideal world to hide out in when you don't want to be disturbed. You would think the planet was uninhabited if not for the spaceport and a few nearby log cabins.

port.name: Landing Pad
port.description: The "spaceport" is a concrete slab forming a large forest clearing surrounded by some log cabins. You see no other parked ships and the area looks deserted.

description.text: This abandoned station appears to have been overtaken by vegetation. But upon closer inspection, the plants are maintained by small robots which keep their growth in check. The internal architecture also suggests it was designed for a species capable of flight. There are doorways that open into wide open areas which are dangerously high from the floor below.

spaceport.text: Although most of the spaceport is empty, there are a surprising amount of ships still docked here. However, a more thorough examination reveals that most are likely not in working condition. Whoever lived here in the past seemed to leave in a panicked rush. Judging from the condition of the station, the evacuation was chaotic and disorganized. There might be something worth salvaging if you look hard enough. You just have to sift through a lot of rusted decaying junk first.

description.text: As the only border crossing between the Rim and the Dirt Belt, authority over the station is in constant dispute. Control over it switches hands often between ambitious pirate warlords. Legend has it that someone once managed to keep their hold over Rum Cellar for an entire year, a historical record that has yet to be broken more than a century after it occurred.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is a ring of docking bays that circle around the station. The internal bulkheads are marred by scorchmarks caused by firefights between rival pirate crews. Some have made bets that the station will be destroyed by the pirates themselves before the navy ever finds it.

description.text: A cloud of cosmic dust has accumulated here. Your atmosphere scanner is detecting some interesting trace elements. What secrets could it be hiding?

description.text: Control of the station has switched hands several times over the centuries. Most of the previous transfers of power were violent. However, the current administration, an organization known as the Red Dragons, bought its way in. They are an independent consortium involved in instellar smuggling operations throughout the galaxy.

spaceport.text: Many of the pirate ships parked here are being repaired. It's a wonder some of them were able to escape the Navy in the condition that they are in. Not everyone here is a pirate. More than a few freighters can be found intermingled with the interceptors and warships. There are also those who conduct business with pirates arriving and departing. Some seek transportation to the planet below while others are engaged in transportation of cargo to and from the station.

description.text: "The Bridge to the Underworld" appears lifeless on the surface. Much of it is a rocky wasteland riddled with canyons and chasms. Supposedly there are secret tunnels hidden within these crevices which lead to vast underground caverns that various pirate gangs use as hideouts.

Bristling with a multitude of weapon mounts, Haiguard appears to be a battle station meant to watch over and protect Oldhome. All the weapons are intact, but non-functional. Whether they were deactivated by the Hai who were operating the station or neutralized by some external force is a matter of contention between Hai and Unfettered historians.
The ancestral capital of the Imperial Hai. Most of the ruins have been hidden away by the encroaching forests, leaving little evidence of their civilization behind.
Much of this world is covered by a raging ocean. The near constant storms have eroded any Hai structures down to their foundations.
The inhabitants of Genesis have developed a pre-hyperdrive civilization. They are attempting to explore space, but the object in orbit over their world prevents them from doing so...

The wreckage of Hai spacecraft are scattered across the land of this desert world. But they are covered by hills of sand. Occasionally, the desert winds will shift these dunes, revealing the derelicts that lie underneath.

This rocky planet has a breathable atmosphere, but food and water are scarce. The rotting wreckage of ancient Hai spacecraft lie smashed upon the surface. Perhaps this system was once a battlefield, much like Wah Ki is today.

This dying world has been cracked open. The cooled mantle still glows with rivers of lava and the core sheds an eerie light upon the rocky outcroppings. Strange interstellar creatures dart across the planet's innards, feasting on its exposed mineral deposits. While there are small traces of various gasses forming a thin atmosphere, many of them are toxic to a human. When the exposed core faces the sun, the heat below the edge of the broken crust exceeds recommended safety limits. With the additional dangers from the hazardous environment and wildlife, a heavy environmental suit is necessary to explore the area.

Centuries after it was built, this station lies mostly forgotten. A small crew is on standby to protect the system, but the available facilities are inadequate for maintaining a proper garrison or offering services to outsiders. As a result, the station rarely gets visitors and the few Unfettered you encounter watch you with suspicion.
The air immediately triggers your gag reflex as it leeches the moisture from your body out through your lungs. Similarly, your eyes itch uncomfortably when exposed to this harsh environment.

Hidden away far from the center of the old empire, the existence of Vade-Kella-Kaska has largely been forgotten by the High Houses. Unlike its sister station, Vade-Osolaa-Kaska, the facilities here have been well maintained by The Shadow House.

description.text: Elos has an abnormally high amount of oxygen in it's atmosphere. Much of it is in the process of bonding with hydrogen produced by microbes floating down from the misty ring above. Computer models indicate that this world will gradually transition from a gas giant to an oceanic one in a few millenia if the microbes continue to thrive at their current pace. By the time this process is complete, it is likely the mist dominating this system will have dissipated.

The ring itself is completely intact with no signs of damage. However, it has been overrun by plasma parasites. The infestation has reached the point where one misplaced blaster shot could set the whole ring on fire...

spaceport.text: The Quarg left nothing obvious to salvage in the empty rooms and corridors of this ring world. It is as if the evacuation was an orderly planned operation. Many sections of the ring are without power. Whether this is because the energy systems are malfunctioning or because the Quarg shut down the generators to preserve them for their eventual return is unknown.

description.text: The flashes of lightning from the nebula above serve as the main source of lighting on the planet's surface. The eerie glow occasionally flickers as activity shifts among the clouds, causing shadows cast by the ruins to dance about wildly.

spaceport.text: A few rusting derelict Quarg ships covered by thick frost occupy some of the other landing pads. Most show signs of combat damage. The corpses nearby give the impression that they were frantically trying to repair one of these ships when something caused an abrupt and violent end to their lives. You're uncertain how many centuries they've been here, but the cold has preserved them well enough for you to discern the twisted horrifying expressions they had on their faces.

description.text: The clouds and their bolts of lightning stop just out of reach of the ringworld shard and the planet below. You're not sure if this facility is responsible for that or if some other invisible force is at work to keep the storm at bay.

spaceport.text: The abandoned spaceport barely has any fuel or spare parts to salvage.

description.text: The purpose of this outpost is clear. A significant portion of its systems are dedicated to special equipment capable of generating a powerful graviton pulse. The Quarloque has been deactivated. It is no longer generating a graviton pulse.

description.text: Other than some isolated patches of grass and shrubs, you find no signs of life on this desolate world. But evidence of an ancient civilization remain. Scattered crystalline ruins stand as a monument to whatever species once called this planet home. The mysterious megaliths tower over you and patterns engraved on some of their surfaces suggest that whoever built them had an understanding of astronomy.

Several asteroids have formed a cluster at this location. Perhaps they are all that remain of a destroyed planet that once occupied this orbital path. With no atmosphere and the sound of micro meteorites tapping your hull a reminder of the danger of asteroid collisions, a heavy environmental suit is necessary to explore the area.

The thick haze from this cloud of cosmic dust obscures your vision of the stars. Your atmosphere scanner is detecting some interesting trace elements. Could anything be hiding deeper within the cloud?

This earth-like planet is covered in decaying ruins. But they don't appear to be Hai ruins. On this world it seems another species evolved, thrived, then died out during the Hai's long absence. Wild animals roam the streets and flying creatures nest in the taller structures. Perhaps this is how Earth would turn out if humans ever abandoned it.
